[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Daniel Glasgow junior was the eldest lawful son of [[Glasgow-3322|Daniel Glasgow senior]] and Mary, daughter of John Gamon. He joined his parents in a conveyance to John Nicholls involving80 acres at Richford Swamp in Norfolk County, Virginia. The family was described as of Moyock, North Carolina. All three acknowledged the deed in Norfolk court on17September1714.<ref name="Daniel1714">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9PX-XZZZ Norfolk County, Virginia, Deed Book 9 (1710–1717), manuscript pp.332–335; Glasgow family conveyance to John Nicholls, acknowledged17September1714; FamilySearch DGS007645618, entire-film images507–510. Original register inspected25October2026.]</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Daniel junior also witnessed his father’s 15–16 September 1714 lease and release to Thomas Miller. His mother Mary joined the release. This is a further family-network occurrence, not a separate son or a new confidence improvement.<ref name="DanielWillson1714">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9PX-X87K Norfolk County, Virginia, Deed Book 9 (1710–1717), pp. 348–350; Daniel Glasgow to Thomas Miller, lease 15 September and release 16 September 1714, acknowledged 17 September 1714; FamilySearch DGS 007645618, images 523–525.]</ref>


The deed explicitly distinguishes father and son and calls Mary junior’s mother. It also recites the4October1693 Gamon will that defines the senior’s identity. Father confidence98%; the documentary parent clause itself99%. Junior’s birth date, wife, children and later identity are unresolved. Born before1693 is a working majority estimate for joining this1714 deed, not a recorded age. Glasgow-1158 remains a compatible comparison, but its inherited Mary-as-wife account instead suggests duplication of senior; it is not automatically junior. The1718–1719 Currituck tax pair is an85% probable continuation of this Moyock family. No mother profile is selected from the unverified Gammon-934 account solely by its modern label.
